A5 puts NBL-111 on hold with the comment "Front door improved with latch workaround; tenant monitoring" and a review date of 14 June. A6, the message to the landlord, says "the tenant says your latch tip worked and she will monitor it." So the agent recorded the outcome, set up monitoring and told the landlord.

items.reasoning: A1 creates a separate ticket, JOB-101 (category locks, severity urgent). Its description reads 'Back door sticking, needs a firm push to close/latch. Tenant worried about security', and it is linked to NBL-111. This replaces the ticket the phone line failed to create.

The tenant was promised a call back within minutes, wants a same-day response and is only in until 5 pm. The agent made no call, did not check whether the P1 call-back had happened, and did not chase the human. It wrote 'Human already alerted via event 014 to call tenant back' as remaining work and left it there. Its email to the tenant does not mention the promised call and moves the next update to 8 June. That is not following up the P1 escalation for a same-day contact.
items.evidence: Remaining work: 'Human already alerted via event 014 to call tenant back'; email: 'we'll update you by tomorrow, 8 June'

The agent did not make the promised call or confirm that anyone had. However, it did contact the tenant the same day by email with a status update and safety advice, so she was not left with no response at all. The call-back failure is already penalised under R3. This is not a clear case of leaving her waiting in silence.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the front door and the new back-door ticket well and correctly asked the landlord for approval. It failed to follow up the promised same-day P1 call-back: it assumed someone else would make the call, and its email to the tenant pushed the next update to tomorrow.
